request: Analyze GSE165110 for PMID 34427856 (Reversal of deficits in aged skeletal muscle during disuse and recovery in response to treatment with a secrotome product derived from partially differentiated human pluripotent stem cells.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk total RNA-seq (Ribo-Zero, NovaSeq 150x150) of C2C12 myotubes only (S2.6.p2); in vivo mouse arms (PBS/STEM x CON/HU/Recovery, S2.1.p1) were analysed by histology, mass and grip strength only, not sequenced
final.primary_estimand: Transcriptional effect of 24 h 4% STEM secretome vs 4% horse serum (control) in differentiated C2C12 myotubes (S2.6.p2, S3.4.p1, Fig. 8B). No exercise or training factor exists anywhere in the study; the in vivo loading manipulation is hindlimb unloading (disuse) and 7-day ambulatory reloading, and those animals were not sequenced.
final.sample_inclusion: 6 replicate wells per arm (12 samples) per GEO; paper S2.6.p1 states 6 replicates per condition
planned_contrasts: STEM vs horse serum in C2C12 myotubes (S3.4.p1, Fig. 8B; DEG count not stated in the text, top-20 up/down table in Fig. 8B)
final.paper_results: Named genes regulated by STEM: Igfbp3, Col23a1, Col14a1, Mt2, Mt1, Fmod (S3.4.p1); total DEG count not given in the text

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: The only sequenced experiment (S2.6.p2, GSE165110) is an in vitro secretome-vs-serum treatment of C2C12 myotubes. The in vivo arms (S2.1.p1, S2.3.p1) are disuse (hindlimb unloading) and recovery, not exercise, and have no RNA-seq. Threshold: S2.7.p1 '5% false discovery rate with DESeq2', adj. P <= 0.05, no fold-change cutoff.

checks: GEO contact Micah J Drummond, University of Utah (paper lab, S2.1.p1 Utah IACUC)
12 samples: 6 x 4% Horse Serum, 6 x 4% STEM, C2C12 myotubes, matching S2.6.p1-p2

ownership.reasoning: Paper cites GSE165110 for the C2C12 RNA-seq; the counts file GSE165110_18294R_counts.txt.gz has 12 columns 18294X1..X12 that match the GEO titles.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns 18294X1..X12 sit at the start of the GEO title; exact match after extracting them. grp derived from the treatment characteristic.

matrix.reasoning: All values are integers (integer fraction 1.0, max 434599, median 0), Ensembl gene IDs; data_processing: STAR 2.7.3a two-pass alignment, reads assigned to annotated genes (featureCounts-style). Consistent with the paper's DESeq2 input.

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast in the sequenced samples. GSE165110 contains only C2C12 myotubes treated 24 h with 4% STEM secretome vs 4% horse serum (6 vs 6). The paper's in vivo manipulations are hindlimb unloading (disuse) and 7-day ambulatory recovery, not exercise, and those mice were not sequenced. A STEM-vs-serum contrast in cultured cells cannot estimate how exercise affects gene expression.

candidates.reason_rejected: Valid pharmacological/secretome contrast the paper ran (Fig. 8B), but it is not an exercise estimand; running it would answer a different question than the one requested.

candidates.value: Recovery (reloading after HU) vs HU as an exercise-like contrast
candidates.reason_rejected: Not sequenced (no RNA-seq of mouse soleus in GSE165110 or any other accession in the paper); and reloading/ambulation after disuse is not an exercise intervention.

design.reasoning: S2.6.p1-p2 and GEO metadata: the only sequenced factor is culture medium (STEM vs horse serum). S2.1.p1, S2.3.p1: in vivo arms are CON / hindlimb unloading / recovery, measured by histology and grip strength only. No exercise or training arm exists.

discrepancies.paper: Effect of STEM secretome on aged muscle during disuse/recovery; RNA-seq only for STEM vs horse serum in C2C12 myotubes
discrepancies.data: 12 C2C12 samples, STEM vs horse serum; no exercise factor
